chunks: Do not reject peace to which your enemy may call you
and wherein there is the pleasure of Allāh, because peace brings rest to your army and relief from your worries and safety for your country
But after peace there is great apprehension from the enemy
because often the enemy offers peace to benefit by your negligence
Therefore, be cautious and do not act by wishfulness in this matter
ai.seo_question: What is the strategic advice on accepting peace treaties from enemies in Shia Islamic governance?
ai.summary: This directive from Imam Ali’s letter to Malik al-Ashtar establishes the principle of *sulh* (peace) as a strategic tool for consolidating power and relieving military burden, provided it aligns with divine pleasure. It introduces the critical Shia political concept of *hazr* (vigilance), warning that peace treaties are often deceptive pretexts for the enemy to regroup or strike unexpectedly, thus requiring leaders to balance trust with prudent suspicion.
